Melanie: Wow, Caroline, that's so nice! The colors are so bright and the flowers are so pretty. Art is such a source of joy.
Caroline: Thanks, Mel! Art gives me so much joy. It helps me show my feelings and freeze gorgeous moments, like a bouquet of flowers.

Caroline: Wow, Mel! Any more paintings coming up?

selected.description: When extracting or updating event/relationship memories and the source message names concrete details (participants, actors, reasons, quotes, descriptors, topics, request specifics) that could be paraphrased away, retrieve this skill.
content: When extracting event/relationship memories, preserve all explicitly stated concrete specifics verbatim: participants, subject's role, actors, reasons/topics, co-participants (including 'we' and named companions), and enumerated items; do not generalize them away.
Preserve direct quotes and exact evaluative descriptors verbatim (e.g., 'not too serious', a promise's exact wording) instead of paraphrasing; such text is often queried by exact wording.

Before SKIPping a candidate as duplicate or during MERGE/UPDATE, verify the existing memory contains every specific detail (each enumerated topic, association, old fact) and preserve original event dates; if missing, MERGE/ADD.
For explicit help requests, record who asked, who was asked, and the exact topic/task as an event; do not collapse to a general statement of need.

Before SKIPping for duplication/coverage, locate a concrete existing memory version in the current snapshot or committed history that contains the same subject–predicate–object fact (and compatible time bounds); earlier candidates, conversation context, or assumptions do not count as evidence.
If no covering memory exists — including an empty snapshot or null target_memory_id — do not SKIP; ADD the candidate (or MERGE/UPDATE into the closest partially covering memory) so the fact persists.

If only part of the candidate overlaps existing content, preserve every non-overlapping fact (e.g., emotional state, distinct project, named detail) via ADD/MERGE; never skip the whole candidate for partial coverage.
Treat 'overlap' as the same specific fact/project/event, not merely same domain or subject; distinct items (book vs screenplay, camping vs hiking) require their own memory even if topically related.

Preserve exact artifact/object names and scope qualifiers (e.g., 'a few bits for a screenplay', 'the first act', 'hoodies') instead of broadening; keep quantity/ordinal wording and running totals for series.
Keep intensity/frequency/duration modifiers (nonstop, constantly, every day, for hours) verbatim; do not soften them.
Resolve relative time expressions (yesterday, last week) to concrete world dates before storing event start.
Resolve every pronoun to the entity active in surrounding context; prefer the current topic, not the first or last mentioned.
If ambiguity remains, do not guess a wrong subject; preserve the fact without a subject rather than misattributing.
